function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity as a natural phenomenon has been known since antiquity (e.g., static electricity from amber). However, systematic study began in the 17th–18th centuries with figures such as William Gilbert, who coined the term “electricus.” Key discoveries include Benjamin Franklin’s kite experiment (1752), Alessandro Volta’s invention of the voltaic pile (1800), and Michael Faraday’s work on electromagnetism (1831). Thus, electricity wasn’t discovered by a single individual but rather developed through contributions from many scientists over time.
